document.abstract: This article will examine how computer assisted drafting (CAD) and computer assisted engineering (CAE) programs are used to streamline television system and facility design. Hardware considerations will be discussed; basic system components will be identified. Typical CAD workstation software will be detailed. System design applications will be shown. An overview of facility architectural design and television system design with and without the use of CAD/CAE software will be presented. Finally a brief case study of the overall design of a mobile teleproduction vehicle will be examined. The use of CAD/CAE in this specialized design area will be discussed.

authors.bio: In 1983, Ed Webster graduated from Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, with a masters of science degree. For the past 15 years he has worked as the chief engineer and/or the design engineer on many interesting and challenging projects. These include designing a production trailer for Multimedia Sports Productions and a post-production studio for Procter & Gamble, being the project manager for a production vehicle for Munwha Broadcasting in Korea, designing a KU-Band uplink for Telespazio in Rome, Italy, and being the design engineer for an auditorium/training complex for the Egyptian Government in Cairo, Egypt. He has also worked as the chief engineer at Midwest International Ltd., Mass Communications for Miami University, and chief engineer for WIFR-TV in Rockford, Illinois. Currently Ed is the manager of engineering for Centro Corp. in Salt Lake City, Utah.

authors.bio: Ron Jones has had a life-long interest in electronics. He began his career in the video industry in the early days of Vital Industry with summer jobs during college. He received his electronics engineering degree in 1971 and has since taken a number of post-graduate engineering classes. Since his graduation, he has been continually employed in broadcast and video-related fields, beginning with Anaconda CATV, a manufacturer of cable TV equipment. He was also employed by Bonneville Broadcasting as a studio engineer and for a number of years by Bosch (now BTS), where he worked on the development of a number of studio-related products. Mr. Jones is currently employed as a senior design engineer at Centre, a major corporation specializing in the design and integration of TV facilities.
